subject: PoC governance & recommended deployment mode — next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finsecure.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: PoC governance & recommended deployment mode — next steps

Hi Emily / Carlos —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. I wanted to summarize our understanding and propose a tightly scoped PoC so you can validate the two critical areas you flagged: data residency/isolation and predictable latency at 95th percentile for your underwriting flows.

Quick recap of what we heard:
- Primary requirement: full network isolation + customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for production PII workloads.
- Performance target: p95 latency <= 150ms for 1–2k concurrent inference qps (batched spikes).
- Timeline: evaluation window of ~4 weeks (trial + production readiness checklist).
- Stakeholders: Emily (security & platform), Carlos (SRE), Tony (ML infra) — please confirm names/roles if I'm missing anyone.

Deployment-mode thoughts (short):
- Hosted API: fastest to start, but does not meet your isolation/KMS requirement without private deployment.
- Dedicated: Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) with customer tenancy improves predictability and separation, but network connectivity and KMS still go through Redwood-managed controls unless combined with Private VPC.
- Private VPC / On-prem: meets isolation + KMS control; requires slightly longer provisioning and a short connectivity/ops onboarding window.

Recommended PoC approach (lean):
1) Week 0: NDA + PoC SOW sign-off (I attached a draft SOW and NDA).
2) Week 1: Security evidence exchange (we'll provide SOC2 reports, architecture diagrams); your security team reviews.
3) Week 2: Private VPC provisioning for a small cluster (single VPC, restricted subnets) + test dataset ingestion (synthetic/hashed).
4) Week 3: Baseline performance run (simulate production QPS) + validation against success criteria.
5) Week 4: Joint review and decision: move to Dedicated reserved capacity or full Private on-prem depending on ops footprint and timeline.

Success criteria (we suggest):
- Security: KMS integration validated and audit logs visible in your SIEM within 48 hours of ingest.
- Performance: p95 token latency <= 150ms at target throughput on your exemplar prompts.
- Reliability: <0.5% error rate during a 24-hour stress window.
- Ops: Deployment runbook + rollback verified by your SRE team.

Next asks from us:
- Please confirm the final stakeholder list (names + emails) for day-to-day PoC coordination.
- If Private VPC is required, confirm if you prefer cloud-managed VPC (we provision) or that we provide an on-prem installer artifact.
- If you can, sign the attached NDA so we can share the SOC2 bundle and KMS integration playbook.

I'll hold a tentative kickoff for Tuesday next week if that works — happy to shift.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
[Attachment: redwood-poc-sow.pdf (PDF, 150KB); NDA_draft.docx (DOCX, 35KB)]

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finsecure.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@finsecure.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 15:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PoC governance & recommended deployment mode — next steps

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for the clear summary. Confirming a few points from our side:
- Security is non-negotiable for the PoC: we need customer-controlled KMS and the ability to route traffic over our VPC endpoints.
- Our SRE lead (Carlos) will validate the network plan, and Tony (not on this thread yet) will run the ML workload validation.
- We can do a 4-week window but would prefer an aggressive Week 0 and Week 1 so the bulk of testing happens in Weeks 2–3.

We are inclined toward Private VPC if Redwood can support a cloud-managed VPC in our AWS account and provide the KMS integration hooks. If that path is materially slower (more than 10 business days to stand up), we might accept Dedicated capacity for an interim validation of latency while we negotiate the VPC details.

I'll ask Carlos to share a quick network contact sheet and the preferred kickoff dates. Also, please share the SOC2 bundle and any architecture diagrams after NDA.

Emily Zhao
Head of Platform Security | FinSecure Inc.
emily.zhao@finsecure.com
[Attachment: none]

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finsecure.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2026 09:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PoC governance & recommended deployment mode — next steps

Thanks for the context, team. A few technical clarifications and a minimal PoC scope we can execute fast: 

Technical clarifications:
- For Private VPC in AWS account: we can provide a CloudFormation/Terraform template that provisions the required subnets, security groups, and endpoints. KMS integration will be via your CMK (we'll request a grant for the Redwood service principal). Typical provisioning time: 2–5 business days after access and IAM role exchange.
- Dedicated capacity (short-term): we can spin a dedicated GPU pool in our tenancy and open a private peering connection; this takes ~48–72 hours but will not give you CMK control — only transit-level isolation.

Minimal PoC scope I propose (can run in parallel):
A) Security onboarding (Day 0–3): NDA, KMS grant, and Exchange of SOC2 artifacts. Vivek will own the SOC2/sensitive evidence bundle delivery.
B) Private VPC quick-provision (Day 3–8): if you approve templates and provide minimal IAM role. We will validate connectivity and a small synthetic workload.
C) Performance run (Day 9–14): run your exemplar prompt set with both 95th percentile and steady-state load tests. We'll collect token-level latency and cost telemetry.

Operational owners:
- Redwood: Dev (technical lead), Vivek (security lead), Soojin (commercial).
- FinSecure: Carlos (SRE), Tony (ML infra), Emily (security).

I'll attach a one-pager checklist (included in the SOW PDF) with the exact logs we will need. If you prefer, we can run the Dedicated route first while the VPC is finalized and then migrate the same workload to Private VPC for final validation.

Cheers,
Dev
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
[Attachment: SOC2-report-2025.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PoC governance & recommended deployment mode — next steps

Perfect — thanks for the quick turn, Emily and Dev.

Action items we will execute immediately:
- I'll send the NDA via DocuSign today (Laurens, looping you for signature tracking).
- Vivek will drop the SOC2 bundle into a secure shared folder after NDA is signed.
- Dev will prepare the Terraform template and a short README for the VPC approach; sharing by Day 3.
- Tentative kickoff: Wed, 11 Aug 2026 — please confirm availability from Carlos and Tony.

If Carlos confirms that a cloud-managed VPC in AWS is acceptable, we'll prioritize that provisioning path. If not, we'll run Dedicated for an interim latency validation and move to Private once network access is ready.

Emily / Carlos — can you confirm the final SRE contact and whether Tony should be on the kickoff? Also, any constraints on test data (PII masking/hashing) so we can prepare the ingest scripts.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
